summary.name: AGENTS
summary.one_liner: AGENTS is an open-source Python library for building, customizing, and deploying autonomous language agents, supporting planning, memory, tool use, multi-agent communication, and symbolic control via SOPs.
use_cases: create multi-agent debate or software company simulations
let a human take part in a multi-agent system
automatically generate agent configs from a task description
summary.what_it_does: The paper presents AGENTS, a library whose core classes (Agent, SOP, Environment) are initialized from a plain-text config file. Agents get long-term memory stored in a vector database with semantic search, plus a short-term working memory (scratchpad). Tool use and web navigation are supported via ToolComponents and OpenAI function calling. Multi-agent systems can use an LLM-based controller for dynamic turn-taking, and any agent can be switched to human control with an is_human flag. Agents can be deployed as APIs with FastAPI, and an automated SOP generation pipeline creates config files from a short task description.
notable: Symbolic control via SOPs (state graphs with transition rules) for more predictable agent behavior
Dynamic scheduling where an LLM controller picks the next agent to act
Agent Hub for sharing and downloading community agents
Human-agent interaction by setting is_human on an agent
caveats: The paper describes a work-in-progress preprint (v3, Dec 2023) and an ongoing effort
Paper's own comparison table is the authors' assessment; the many listed features depend on LLM access (e.g., OpenAI GPT APIs)
